purpose: Reference dataset for 3D eyewear asset generation. Seven real frames from the supplier catalog, every published photo of each plus a full descriptor.

conventions.origin: Midpoint of the bridge on the front face of the frame

confidence_levels.observed_in_photos: Read off the reference photos by eye.
confidence_levels.estimated: Computed from supplier data by a stated formula.
confidence_levels.heuristic: Typical value for this construction type. Not measured. Do not treat as spec.

image_note: One photo per colourway is everything the supplier has. All of a model's photos share the same three-quarter angle (SL906 is the exception: its single JPEG holds a three-quarter and a front shot), so extra colourways give texture variation, not parallax.

frames.selected_because: Thick acetate full-rim rectangle — the baseline case: large flat surfaces, visible bevel, chunky temples.
Injected plastic cat-eye with two-tone layering — tests non-convex silhouette and a colour split that is not a material split.
Combo build: acetate round front with thin gold metal temples — two materials, two very different cross-sections in one model.
Wire-rim aviator with a brow bar — thin tubular geometry and a double bridge, the hardest silhouette to reconstruct from a single photo.
Semi-rimless (nylor): metal upper rim and a nylon cord holding the lens underneath — the lens edge is the visible silhouette, not the frame.
Three-piece rimless titanium — no rim at all, lenses drilled and bolted. Also the only frame here whose photo already ships two camera views.
Metal navigator with a brow bar and plastic temples — square wire rim, two-tone anodising, mixed materials at the end piece.
